title: Create a disposable local account
goal: Create and verify a locked local account with a usable home and Bash shell.
challenge: Create locked ll-u2 with home /home/ll-u2, own primary group and /bin/bash. Verify that the intended user can create a small home file, inspect the result and safely remove only this fixture. Do not set credentials or grant sudo.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-u2 && ! getent group ll-u2 && test ! -e /home/ll-u2 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-u2
steps.explanation: Fail closed if this disposable name or home exists. -m creates a home from /etc/skel; -U creates a primary group; no password is set.
steps.expected: Fresh account ll-u2, same-named primary group, home and Bash shell. A nonzero status/collision means stop setup.

steps.command: getent passwd ll-u2; ls -ld /home/ll-u2; sudo passwd -S ll-u2
steps.explanation: Inspect explicit choices instead of assuming distribution defaults. Locked passwords are intentional here.
steps.expected: Home belongs to ll-u2; shell is /bin/bash; password status L.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-u2 -- bash -c 'cd "$HOME" && printf "owned\n" > note.txt && pwd && id'
steps.explanation: The nested command executes inside the guest as ll-u2. Single quotes keep $HOME for that user's Bash.
steps.expected: Directory /home/ll-u2 and non-root ll-u2 identity; note created.

steps.command: sudo stat -c "%U:%G %a" /home/ll-u2/note.txt; sudo runuser -u ll-u2 -- cat /home/ll-u2/note.txt
steps.explanation: Verify actual write/read access and ownership. Creating an account is not permission to authenticate without credentials.
steps.expected: Owner ll-u2 and content owned; ordinary text file has no execute bit.

hints: useradd without -m may leave a home path in the database but no created directory.
Use an explicit shell and inspect it; do not alter learner.
A root-created file in that home can still be root-owned. Run the creation as the new user.
review: Retain home/shell/locked-status evidence and successful file creation/read under ll-u2.
Explain why this proves home access, not password authentication.
coverage: LPIC-1 107.1 local account creation/removal. Partial coverage; original material, self-review only. No automatic assessment or full LPIC preparation.
